problem_statement: The paper frames the task as financial generative modeling with quantum circuit Born machines, specifically modeling daily changes in Japanese government bond interest rates. It presents this as a real-data generative modeling problem for interest rate time series.
problem_statement_quotes: We evaluate our method on a financial modeling task involving daily changes in Japanese government bond (JGB) interest rates.
The generative modeling task in this work focuses on interest rate time series.

Following [1], we use Japanese Government Bond (JGB) rates instead of more commonly used foreign exchange datasets, as interest rates exhibit stronger temporal and cross-maturity correlations due to the yield curve structure.
classical_baseline: The paper compares its LLM-generated ansatz against the standard TwoLocal ansatz from Qiskit as the baseline QCBM architecture. It also frames prior work as mostly using simulators with minimal comparisons to classical baselines or real hardware.
classical_baseline_quotes: As a baseline, we employ the TwoLocal ansatz from Qiskit as the QCBM architecture.
The baseline model uses the same number of qubits and training configuration as our method, allowing for a fair comparison of generative performance.

Separately, prior studies on QCBMs [1], [2] have demonstrated their capability to model simple datasets such as bars-and-stripes and interest rate time series. However, these studies are typically limited to simulators, with minimal comparisons to classical baselines or deployment on real hardware.
classical_difficulty: The paper says the main difficulty is that practical deployment is challenged by hardware noise and the limited adaptability of standard ansatz templates. It also states that transpilation can substantially increase circuit depth, which worsens noise sensitivity and makes execution on current processors harder.
classical_difficulty_quotes: However, practical deployment remains challenging due to hardware noise and the limited adaptability of standard ansatz templates.
Transpilation often increases circuit depth substantially, exacerbating noise sensitivity and hindering execution on current quantum processors.
While LLMs effectively guide ansatz generation and consistently reduce the MMD loss per iteration, they sometimes produce invalid or unsupported circuit components, especially after 10–20 iterations.
business_stakes: The paper emphasizes near-term hardware feasibility and deployability rather than explicit business or regulatory stakes. It says reducing transpilation overhead and controlling circuit depth improves the feasibility of deploying generated ansatz on real devices.
business_stakes_quotes: Incorporating hardware details such as qubit connectivity and error rates into LLM prompts reduces transpilation overhead and controls circuit depth, improving the feasibility of deploying generated ansatz on real devices
These findings demonstrate the practical utility of LLM-driven quantum architecture search and highlight a promising path toward robust, deployable generative models for near-term quantum devices.
extraction_notes: Motivation is explicit in abstract, introduction, and limitations; framing is mostly algorithmic but includes a clear financial time-series task.
